q: 1. The horizontal thrust due to rise in temperature in a semi circular two hinged arch of radius R is proportional to
explain: Analysis shows that for a two-hinged semicircular arch, the temperature-induced horizontal thrust is inversely proportional to R² (since it depends on flexibility, which grows with R³, against expansion which grows with R).

q: 2. While using three moments equations, a fixed end of a continuous beam is replaced by an additional span of
explain: To apply the three-moment theorem at a fixed support, it is modeled as an imaginary additional span of zero length attached beyond the fixed end.

q: 3. Three hinged arch will have three hinges
options: two at the two ends and one any where in between the two ends
two at the two ends and one at the crown only
one hinge at the crown essentially and the other two any where
explain: A standard three-hinged arch features two hinges at the supports (abutments) and a third hinge at the highest point, known as the crown.

q: 4. The statically indeterminate structure can be solved by
options: ignoring all deformations and assuming the structure to be rigid
using the equations of statics and the necessary number of equations of compatibility
explain: Indeterminate structures require both equilibrium equations (statics) and displacement-based equations (compatibility) to be fully solved.

q: 5. A prop is
options: An additional support provided to a stable structure to avoid any displacement at the desired point in a direction perpendicular to the plane of the prop
the support which gives the maximum number of reactions for the stability of the structure
a support which will not affect the geometry of the deformed structure
a dummy support provided for architectural purposes
explain: A prop is a redundant support (often a roller or hinge) added to a structure to reduce deflection or provide extra stability at a specific point.

q: 6. A rigid prop is one which
options: permits 50% of free deflection, that would have occurred if the prop were not there
does not permit any displacement perpendicular to that plane of prop
supports the entire load and relieves all other supports completely
explain: A rigid prop acts as an unyielding support, meaning the vertical displacement (deflection) at the point of the prop is forced to be zero.

q: 7. DSI of structure depends upon
explain: DSI is a geometric property determined by the arrangement of members and the types of joints (rigid vs. pinned) and supports.

q: 8. The moment distribution method is formulated by
explain: Hardy Cross published the Moment Distribution Method in 1930, providing a simple iterative way to analyze indeterminate structures.

q: 9. A parabolic cable is subjected to a rise of t°C in temperature. Then the increase in dip of the cable is proportional to
explain: The extra length gained due to thermal expansion relates to dip change through a relation involving the square of the span, giving increase in dip proportional to (span)².

q: 10. Which of the following methods of structure analysis is a force method?
explain: Column Analogy and Method of Consistent Deformation are Force Methods (Flexibility Methods), where redundant forces are the unknowns. Slope Deflection and Moment Distribution are Displacement Methods.

q: 11. Degree of static indeterminacy of the frame is equal to (refer to image 1666)
explain: Calculated using $D_s = 3c - r'$, where 'c' is the number of closed loops and 'r' represents the releases at supports or hinges.

q: 12. Portal method of framed analysis for horizontal loads is appropriate for a frame:
options: that has a width greater than its height
that has a height greater than its width
explain: The portal method is an approximate method suitable for low-rise frames where the width is significant relative to the height.

q: 13. The effective length of a column with both ends fixed is
explain: For a column fixed at both ends, the effective length is Le = L/2, per Euler's standard end-condition factors.

q: 14. Unequal settlement in the supports of statically indeterminate structure develop
explain: Settlement in indeterminate structures induces internal forces and reactions that wouldn't exist in a determinate structure.

q: 15. The moment distribution method is best suited for
explain: as per key 1 MDM is specifically designed for rigid frames and continuous beams where joint rotations occur.

q: 16. In the moment distribution method, the sum of distribution factors of all the members meeting at any joint is always :
explain: The total unbalanced moment must be 100% distributed, so $\sum DF = 1$.

q: 17. In the Euler's theory for long columns it is assumed that
options: the failure occurs by crushing of the material
the failure occurs by buckling only
the column shortens so much that it will become a short column
the column is having initial curvature and the load is eccentrically applied
explain: Euler's column theory is based purely on elastic instability (buckling) failure, ignoring crushing/direct stress effects, applicable to long columns.

q: 18. What is principle of virtual work?
options: work done by external forces > internal forces
work done by external forces < internal forces
work done by external forces = work done by internal forces
explain: For a system in equilibrium, the virtual work done by external forces equals the virtual work done by internal forces.

q: 19. The statically indeterminate structures can be solved by
options: ignoring all deformations and assuming the structure to be rigid
using the equations of static and the necessary number of equations of compatibility
explain: Statically indeterminate structures require both the equilibrium (static) equations and additional compatibility equations (based on deformation) to be solved fully.

q: 20. A dam is a
explain: A dam has all three dimensions (length, height, and thickness/width) of comparable significant magnitude, making it a three-dimensional structure.

q: 21. An internally indeterminate structure
options: may be unstable structure based on supports
explain: Internal indeterminacy (redundant members) is independent of external support conditions; depending on the supports provided, the overall structure may even be unstable.

q: 22. If M is the external moment which rotates the near end of a prismatic beam without translation ( the far end being fixed), then the moment induced at the far end is
options: M/2 in same direction as M
M/2 in opposite direction as M
explain: The carry-over factor for a prismatic member with the far end fixed is 1/2, meaning half the applied moment M is carried over to the far end in the same rotational sense.

q: 23. A simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load over its whole span, is propped at the centre of the span so that the beam is held to the level of the end supports. The reaction of the prop will be
explain: For a beam propped at midspan and brought level with the end supports under UDL, standard analysis gives the prop reaction as 5/8 of the total distributed load.

q: 24. A rigid jointed plane frame is stable and statically determinate ............. .
explain: For a rigid-jointed plane frame (each joint with 3 dof), the condition for stable and statically determinate structure is 3m + r = 3j.

q: 25. The number of independent equations to be satisfied for static equilibrium in a space structure is
explain: A three-dimensional (space) structure requires 6 independent equilibrium equations: 3 force equations (ΣFx, ΣFy, ΣFz) and 3 moment equations (ΣMx, ΣMy, ΣMz).

q: 26. The degree of static indeterminacy of a rigid jointed space frame is given by
explain: For a rigid-jointed space frame, each member has 6 internal force components and each joint provides 6 equilibrium equations, giving static indeterminacy = 6m + r − 6j.

q: 27. The principle of virtual work can be applied to elastic system by considering the virtual work of
options: internal as well as external force
explain: The principle of virtual work for elastic systems equates the virtual work done by external forces to the virtual work (strain energy) done by internal forces, so both must be considered.

q: 28. Castigliano's first theorem is applicable
options: only when principle of superposition is valid
explain: Castigliano's first theorem, which relates partial derivatives of strain energy to displacements, is applicable specifically when the principle of superposition (linear elastic behavior) holds.

q: 29. A multi span continuous beam is simply supported at the two ends. One of the intermediate supports sinks with respect to other supports. Due to this settlement, the bending moment will get modified at
options: only the two supports adjacent to the one that sinks
all the supports except the two end supports
explain: Support settlement in a continuous beam affects the bending moments at all intermediate supports (due to the continuity/redundancy), but the two simply supported end supports (already zero moment) remain unaffected.

q: 30. For a two hinged arch, if one of the support settles horizontally, then the horizontal thrust .............
explain: A horizontal settlement (moving the supports apart) reduces the strain energy stored due to the thrust, effectively decreasing the induced horizontal thrust.

q: 31. In column analogy method, the area of an analogous column for a fixed beam of span L and flexural rigidity EI is taken as
explain: In the column analogy method, the analogous column's cross-sectional area is taken as L/EI, corresponding to the M/EI diagram base.

q: 32. The deflection at any point of a perfect frame can be obtained by applying a unit load at the joint in
options: the direction in which the deflection is required
explain: The unit load method (virtual work) requires the unit load to be applied at the point and in the exact direction of the deflection being sought.

q: 33. In slope deflection equations, the deformations are considered to be caused by
options: both shear force and bending moment
explain: The slope-deflection method idealizes members as being deformed (bent) due to bending moment only, neglecting shear and axial deformations.

q: 34. The three moments equation is applicable only when
options: there is no settlement of supports
there is no discontinuity such as hinges within the span
explain: Clapeyron's three-moment theorem requires continuity of the beam (no internal hinges/discontinuities) between the spans considered, though it can handle varying EI, unequal spans, and support settlements with modified forms.

q: 35. For structural carbon steel the ratio of yield stress to ultimate strength will be about
explain: For typical structural carbon (mild) steel, the yield-to-ultimate strength ratio is commonly around 0.55 to 0.6.

q: 36. In moment distribution method, the sum of distribution factors of all the members meeting at any joint is always
explain: By definition, distribution factors at a joint are proportional shares of the total stiffness, and their sum must always equal 1 (100% of the unbalanced moment is distributed).

q: 37. The carryover factor in a prismatic member whose far end is fixed is
explain: For a prismatic member with the far end fixed, the carryover factor (fraction of moment transmitted to the far end) is 1/2, a standard moment-distribution constant.

q: 38. The carryover factor in a prismatic member whose far end is hinged is
explain: If the far end of a member is hinged (cannot resist moment), no moment can be carried over there, so the carryover factor is zero.

q: 39. In slope deflection method, the unknown rotations at various joints are determined by considering
explain: In the slope-deflection method, unknown joint rotations are solved for by writing and satisfying the moment equilibrium equations at each joint.

q: 40. In a rigid jointed frame, the rotation of various members meeting at a joint will be
options: proportional to the length of member
proportional to respective moment of inertia
explain: Since a rigid joint rotates as a single unit, all members rigidly connected at that joint undergo the same (equal) angle of rotation.
